function: Learned RIS phase shifts (TD3, maximizing weighted capacity) and federated multiagent DDPG allocation of vehicle transmit power and local CPU frequency (minimizing AoI plus energy) (pp. 6-9).
system: 50 single-antenna vehicles, multiantenna BS with edge server, passive reflecting RIS (M=100, 3-bit phases), LoS plus Rician RIS links, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 5, 11).
method: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning: upper-layer TD3 for RIS phases at the BS; lower-layer FMADDPG with per-vehicle agents, federated parameter averaging and attention critic; RIS-trajectory pretraining (pp. 6-11).
data_channel: Custom simulated 3-D geometric channel: LoS path loss (exponent 2.5, beta0=1e-3), Rician RIS-vehicle fading, simulated vehicle mobility; no 3GPP model or measured data (pp. 4-5, 11).
test_conditions: Trained 1000 episodes of 1000 steps in one simulator; results are training curves and sweeps of RIS size, arrival rate, payload, power; trained-agent reuse not stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: SAC, QMIX; non-learned: block coordinate descent, random RIS with random allocation, no RIS with random allocation (p. 11).
metrics: Reward, AoI (ms), total and per-user power consumption (W), V2V payload transmission success probability, sum of V2I AoI and V2I rates (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Measured training runtime per episode: about 15 s for TD3 and 28 s for FMADDPG on an RTX 4090 workstation; no FLOPs, parameter count or inference time (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "The proposed channel model is illustrated in Fig. 2"; p. 5: "accounts for the Rician fading between the RIS and vehicle k". It is a custom 3-D geometric simulator (LoS path loss exponent 2.5 plus a Rician RIS link); no 3GPP model or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "under different numbers of RIS elements during the TD3-based RIS phase optimization process" are reward curves of separate training runs (Fig. 4, p. 12); the sweeps of Figs. 7-10 (pp. 12-13) do not say that a trained agent is tested on a configuration it was not trained on.
q3_support: p. 11: "SAC [30], QMIX [34]" and "Random RIS with Random RA" are the benchmarks, with BCD; p. 12: "significantly outperforming SAC, QMIX, BCD, and the two random strategies" on AoI, with power and rate comparisons in Figs. 7-10.
q4_support: p. 11: "The average runtime per episode is approximately 15 s for the TD3 component and 28 s for the FMADDPG component". This is the training runtime per episode only; no operation or parameter count is given.
q5_support: p. 11: "The algorithms are implemented in Python with PyTorch 2.0"; channels and mobility are simulated and no link to code or data is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 3 because the learned physical-layer function is the RIS phase configuration (TD3, p. 7); FMADDPG learns vehicle transmit power and local CPU frequency, a computing decision admitted jointly with a physical-layer one. FMADDPG averages agent parameters digitally (Eq. 20, p. 9), not over the air, so it is not area 7. The conclusion says RIS phase control is ideal and continuous (p. 14) while Table I gives 3-bit phases (p. 11). Figs. 9-10 report V2V payload, V2I AoI and V2I rates, which the system model of Section II never defines. Q4 rests on the measured training runtime per episode, a borderline cost. Tables I-II and Figs. 4-10 were read from the page images (pp. 11-13).
